answer: A graduated identity cost curve prices each new agent identity by active identities sharing its funding source, and an atlas of those sources sets the multiplier. Agents can wander across providers, but source fingerprints persist, so splitting payments raises marginal fees instead of resetting them. When a funding source reaches tundra-scale counts, the next identity costs $50, then $200, then $800, forcing an attacker to fund every alias at rising real cost.
